beats.act: cold open
beats.narration_text: Konnichiwa — this is Liam, in for Bear. Ask an agent to rewrite a chapter and it hands you something fluent back immediately. The harder skill isn't generating the rewrite — it's judging one. Two voices, one diff, one verdict with quotes. Let's do the exercise properly.

send arms, runningText plays

props.command: Walk me through how to properly judge an AI's rewrite of a chapter in a different voice — not just accept it.
output: a voice is a spec file, not a prompt

beats.act: Act I — A Voice Is a File, Not a Vibe
beats.narration_text: Seven registers exist for the same book, and none of them is the 'right' one. Wonder. Generic. Socratic. Sardonic. Narrative. Pragmatist. Teardown. The book underneath never changes — only which mask reads it back to you.

beats.act: Act I — A Voice Is a File, Not a Vibe
beats.narration_text: A voice lives in a file, not a prompt. Every voice has a folder, voices slash its name, and a VOICE dot M-D inside it — a specification with a conversion contract: what must survive the rewrite untouched, and how everything else gets transformed.

beats.act: Act I — A Voice Is a File, Not a Vibe
beats.narration_text: Four of the seven shipped voices. Wonder strips to one hook, no added exercises. Generic stays warm and neutral, definition then example then practice. Socratic tells you almost nothing — questions, surfaced confusion, you reason it out. Sardonic drops footnote jokes into hard problems.

show.event: four chips snap in: Wonder, Generic, Socratic, Sardonic

items: Socratic — tells you nothing, you reason it out
Sardonic — dry, footnote jokes, hard problems
props.caption: four of the seven shipped voices

beats.act: Act I — A Voice Is a File, Not a Vibe
beats.narration_text: The remaining three. Narrative tells the discovery story — who was wrong first. Pragmatist wants a formula, then practice problems, zero personality. Teardown takes the chapter apart and judges its own design choices. Every one of them writes only into voices, never into chapters.

show.event: three chips snap in: Narrative, Pragmatist, Teardown

items: Teardown — judges its own design choices
props.caption: originals in chapters/ are never touched

beats.act: Act I — A Voice Is a File, Not a Vibe
beats.narration_text: Pick two voices for the exercise, and the choice already decides how much you'll learn. Two similar registers barely disagree with each other. Socratic against Pragmatist refuses to agree on anything — one tells you nothing, the other tells you everything and drills it.

beats.act: Act I — A Voice Is a File, Not a Vibe
beats.narration_text: There's no single good voice — only good for this reader, doing this job. That line is the whole chapter, and you won't actually believe it until you watch two voices fight over the same paragraph.

beats.act: Act II — Diff the Change, Not the Charm
beats.narration_text: Read the pretty rewrite and nod, and you've learned nothing — that's taste, not evidence. Diff it against the original instead, and you can see exactly what was added, what got cut, which claims were quietly softened.

show.event: two tracks diverge: reading-and-nodding arcs up warn, diffing arcs down good

tracks.label: Diff against the original

beats.act: Act II — Diff the Change, Not the Charm
beats.narration_text: The diff is the evidence. Every insertion, every deletion, every softened claim sits right there on the page, in a form you can actually argue about — instead of a feeling you can't.

shot.prompt: real archival copyedited-manuscript photo -- illustrative of the diff as evidence, not a literal depiction. Already sourced, see media/A2-3.source.txt

show.event: treated plate; slow push into the copyedit marks
serif label lands: 'the diff is the evidence'

beats.act: Act II — Diff the Change, Not the Charm
beats.narration_text: Mark three specific changes per rewrite: better, worse, or neutral — for the reader your Blueprint named, not in the abstract. A deleted definition isn't universally worse. It depends entirely on who's reading it and why.

beats.act: Act II — Diff the Change, Not the Charm
beats.narration_text: Same deleted definition, two verdicts. For a reference-seeker: worse — the fact they needed is just gone. For a concept-builder: better — the question it left behind does more work than the sentence did. The reader decides which one is yours.

beats.act: Act III — The Verdict Needs Quotes
beats.narration_text: The deliverable isn't the rewrite. It's a two-hundred word verdict — which voice serves your reader, and why, quoting the exact passages that prove it. Cite or it doesn't count.

beats.act: Act III — The Verdict Needs Quotes
beats.narration_text: One real sentence, rewritten twice, from an actual run of this exercise: 'A finished book, in this system, is not a Word document you email around.' Watch what each voice does to it.

beats.act: Act III — The Verdict Needs Quotes
beats.narration_text: The diff-level judgment: Socratic removed the mechanism and added a question. Pragmatist removed the voice — the 'email around' image — and added a formula. Neither rewrite is free; each one traded something specific for something else.

beats.act: Act III — The Verdict Needs Quotes
beats.narration_text: Against a nervous first-time builder's actual job — learning that a change travels to the artifact — the verdict lands: lead Socratic, land Pragmatist. Open with the gap-exposing question; close with the mechanism once they're already building.

beats.act: Act III — The Verdict Needs Quotes
beats.narration_text: That verdict is only defensible because it quotes the two changes. Delete the quotes, and 'lead Socratic, land Pragmatist' is just an opinion again — the citation is the entire difference between a judgment and a guess.

beats.act: Act IV — What Goes Wrong
beats.narration_text: Four ways this exercise quietly fails — and every single one of them is a shortcut around the diff, not a mistake in the rewrite itself.

shot.prompt: real archival warning-signs photo -- illustrative of what goes wrong, not a literal depiction. Already sourced, see media/A4-1.source.txt

show.event: treated plate; slow push onto the signs

beats.act: Act IV — What Goes Wrong
beats.narration_text: The agent edits chapters directly — it ignored the write-only-to-voices rule, and the evidence is gone. You read the rewrite and 'liked it' — taste, not a diff. The verdict has no quotes — a vibe. Both voices 'seem fine' — you picked two that don't fight.

show.event: four chips snap in, one per symptom

items: You read the rewrite and 'liked it'
props.caption: every one is a shortcut around the diff

beats.act: Act IV — What Goes Wrong
beats.narration_text: 'The verdict has no quotes' sounds like a style note. It isn't — a rewrite claim without a quote is unfalsifiable. There's no way to check it, agree with it, or argue against it. The fix: cite the specific line, every single time.

show.event: question card: 'style note, or something worse?'
two outcomes: sounds minor / actually unfalsifiable

data.question: Is 'no quotes' just a style note?

branches.label: It's actually unfalsifiable
branches.detail: no way to check, agree, or argue with it
branches.fix: cite the specific line, every time

resolver.label: It's not style
resolver.detail: it's whether the claim can be checked at all

beats.act: Act IV — What Goes Wrong
beats.narration_text: Every fix is the same fix, wearing four outfits: stop the agent, diff against the original, judge the changes, cite the lines. Skip any one step and the exercise degrades straight back into reading a rewrite and liking it.

show.event: four chips snap in: Stop, Diff, Judge, Cite

props.caption: skip one step and it degrades back into 'liking it'

beats.act: Act IV — What Goes Wrong
beats.narration_text: This is the exact muscle a much bigger gate will demand later — the human rewrite that turns a starter into your own book, the one no agent is ever allowed to sign. Directing and judging an AI's voice here is the rehearsal for judging your own.

beats.act: Act IV — What Goes Wrong
beats.narration_text: Your book has a voice you can choose deliberately now. What it still doesn't have is the study layer — the quizzes, exercises, flashcards a student can actually practice against. That's next: build them, then audit them for the ones that quietly fail.

beats.act: verdict
beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. A voice is a specification in voices, name, VOICE dot M-D — a conversion contract naming what survives the rewrite and what transforms, across seven shipped registers from Wonder to Teardown. The deliverable is a diff, not a read: pick two voices that genuinely fight, then mark each change better, worse, or neutral for the reader your Blueprint named, never in the abstract. A verdict without a quoted line is unfalsifiable — the real worked example, Socratic versus Pragmatist on one sentence, is only defensible because it cites exactly what each rewrite added and removed. And every failure mode in this exercise is the same shortcut: skipping the diff. Stop the agent, diff against the original, judge the changes, cite the lines — the rehearsal for the human-rewrite gate no agent may ever sign.

Every failure mode here is the same shortcut, skipping the diff: stop the agent, diff against the original, judge the changes, cite the lines — the rehearsal for the human-rewrite gate.

beats.act: your turn handoff
beats.narration_text: Your turn — here's the prompt, read it with me. 'Take one chapter or document I've already written, and rewrite it in two voices that genuinely disagree. Diff each rewrite against my original, mark three changes in each as better, worse, or neutral for my actual reader — and write me a verdict with the exact lines quoted as evidence.' Run it. Liam, in for Bear.
